question: Are barefoot shoes good for your feet?

say: You're thinking about buying barefoot shoes, which means paying money to feel like you're wearing no shoes.
Let's see if your feet actually need them.
Your feet were built with twenty-six bones each, three arches and small muscles that help hold those arches up.
Like any muscle, they get stronger when you make them work.
When runners walked in flat, flexible shoes for eight weeks, their foot muscles got about forty percent stronger, and simple foot exercises worked just as well, for free.
Runners who did foot exercises for eight weeks, and kept them up, even got fewer running injuries over the next year.
When runners switched to running in toe shoes over ten weeks, more than half showed bone stress on their scans.
The plan that made feet stronger had people walk in flat, flexible shoes, not run, building up from two and a half thousand steps a day to five thousand, then seven.
If your feet are painful, stiff, weak or numb, you keep injuring them or losing your balance, or one foot has gone flat, see a doctor, not a shoe shop.
Let's get you back to factory settings.
